hook.en: Glycolysis releases only a small part of the energy in glucose. Inside the mitochondria, pyruvic acid is stripped of all its carbon as CO₂ and its hydrogen is handed to carriers.
hook.kn: ಗ್ಲೈಕೋಲಿಸಿಸ್ ಗ್ಲೂಕೋಸ್‌ನ ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ಸಣ್ಣ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಮೈಟೋಕಾಂಡ್ರಿಯದೊಳಗೆ ಪೈರುವಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲದ ಎಲ್ಲ ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ CO₂ ಆಗಿ ಹೊರಬರುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಹೈಡ್ರೋಜನ್ ವಾಹಕಗಳಿಗೆ ಹಸ್ತಾಂತರವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Glycolysis releases only a small part of the energy in glucose. Inside the mitochondria, pyruvic acid is stripped of all its carbon as CO₂ and its hydrogen is handed to carriers.

body.en: Aerobic respiration, the complete oxidation of organic substances in the presence of oxygen, takes place within the mitochondria. Pyruvate formed in the cytoplasm enters the mitochondrial matrix and undergoes oxidative decarboxylation by the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, which needs several coenzymes including NAD⁺ and coenzyme A. Pyruvic acid + CoA + NAD⁺ → acetyl CoA + CO₂ + NADH + H⁺. Two molecules of NADH are produced from the metabolism of two pyruvic acids (one glucose).

points.en: Per glucose: 2 acetyl CoA, 2 CO₂, 2 NADH.

narration.kn: ಪೈರುವೇಟ್ ಮೈಟೋಕಾಂಡ್ರಿಯದ ಮಾತೃಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪೈರುವಿಕ್ ಡಿಹೈಡ್ರೋಜಿನೇಸ್‌ನಿಂದ ಅಸಿಟೈಲ್ CoA ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ; CO₂ ಮತ್ತು NADH ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

narration.en: Let us draw the link reaction and then go round the Krebs cycle counting what comes out.

say.en: In the mitochondrial matrix, pyruvic acid loses a CO₂ and is oxidised, giving acetyl CoA and NADH. This link reaction needs pyruvate dehydrogenase.
Acetyl CoA joins oxaloacetic acid to form citric acid, the first product of the cycle.
Going round, citric acid loses two CO₂ to reach succinyl CoA, then OAA is rebuilt via malic acid.
Each turn gives 2 CO₂, 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ and 1 GTP. One glucose gives two pyruvates, so the cycle turns twice.

text.en: Per turn: 2 CO₂, 3 NADH, FADH₂, GTP

prompt.kn: ಪೈರುವಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲದಿಂದ ಕ್ರೆಬ್ಸ್ ಚಕ್ರದ ಹಂತಗಳನ್ನು ಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಜೋಡಿಸಿ.

steps.en: Pyruvic acid → acetyl CoA in the matrix (1 NADH, 1 CO2): the link reaction
Acetyl CoA + oxaloacetic acid → citric acid (citrate synthase)
Citric acid is isomerised to isocitrate
α-Ketoglutaric acid → succinyl CoA (1 NADH, 1 CO2)
Succinyl CoA → succinic acid (1 GTP, which gives 1 ATP)
Succinic acid → malic acid via fumaric acid (1 FADH2)
Malic acid → oxaloacetic acid (1 NADH); the cycle continues

explanation.en: Per pyruvic acid the link reaction and the cycle release 3 CO2 and make 4 NADH, 1 FADH2 and 1 ATP. Oxaloacetic acid is regenerated, so the cycle can accept the next acetyl CoA.

body.en: The cycle was first elucidated by Hans Krebs. The acetyl group condenses with oxaloacetic acid (OAA, 4C) and water to form citric acid (6C), catalysed by citrate synthase, releasing CoA. Citrate is isomerised to isocitrate, followed by two successive decarboxylations to α-ketoglutaric acid and then succinyl-CoA. The rest of the cycle converts succinyl-CoA back to OAA. The conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinic acid is accompanied by synthesis of one GTP (substrate-level phosphorylation), which in a coupled reaction can make ATP from ADP. In each turn there are three points where NAD⁺ is reduced to NADH + H⁺ and one point where FAD is reduced to FADH₂. The cycle continues only with continued oxidation of NADH and FADH₂ and regeneration of NAD⁺ and FAD.

points.en: Per turn: 2 CO₂, 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂, 1 GTP.

narration.kn: ಕ್ರೆಬ್ಸ್ ಚಕ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಸಿಟೈಲ್ ಗುಂಪು OAA ಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಸೇರಿ ಸಿಟ್ರಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಸುತ್ತಿನಲ್ಲಿ 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ ಮತ್ತು 1 GTP ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತವೆ; ಒಂದು ಗ್ಲೂಕೋಸ್‌ಗೆ ಎರಡು ಸುತ್ತು.

problem.en: Count the products of the link reaction and the Krebs cycle for one glucose molecule.

steps.en: One glucose gives 2 pyruvate, so the link reaction runs twice: 2 NADH and 2 CO₂.
The Krebs cycle turns twice: 2 × (3 NADH + 1 FADH₂ + 1 GTP + 2 CO₂) = 6 NADH, 2 FADH₂, 2 GTP, 4 CO₂.
Total from pyruvate onwards: 8 NADH, 2 FADH₂, 2 GTP and 6 CO₂ (all 6 carbons of glucose).
